ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution with approximately 85% high-intensity white pixels and 15% low-intensity black/dark grey pixels primarily localized at the periphery and peduncle junction.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white macro-regions across both lobes; a continuous black boundary layer (5-15 pixels wide) following the trailing edge; a vertical dark pigmentation band extending from the peduncle through the center of the fluke; scattered dark focal spots (2-5 pixel diameter) distributed across the mid-section of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped central depression with a calculated angle of approximately 52 degrees and a depth of roughly 12% relative to the vertical lobe height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations along the entire trailing edge boundary; presence of distinct jagged peaks and troughs with variable pixel-amplitude; notable deeper indentation located approximately 20% inward from the left distal tip.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strong convex curve originating from the median notch, transitioning to a sharper upward sweep at the distal lobe tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple dark, roughly circular pixel clusters concentrated on the right lobe; small white high-contrast clusters visible on the dark peduncle surface near the water line.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several unaligned dark linear disruptions; a prominent diagonal scrape on the upper right lobe and multiple faint horizontal rake-like marks on the central-left lobe area.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Localized dark scarring and irregular pigmentation at the fluke-peduncle insertion point; multiple visible rake marks across the right fluke lobe.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique 'ink-blot' style dark pigmentation pattern extending from the base of the fluke into the central white regions of both lobes.
